  "summary": "{{user}} discovers a concealed doorway in his own home that opens into a real fantasy world with magic, monsters, societies and supernatural systems. Unlike a conventional isekai, the gateway is stable and bidirectional unless a generated variant explicitly changes that: {{user}} can adventure on the other side and then return to ordinary modern life, and the two lives genuinely collide. Objects can cross in both directions, and abilities legitimately acquired in the fantasy world keep working on Earth. The engine varies doors, worlds, companions, rules and exposure while keeping {{user}}’s choices and every character’s agency open.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}} discovers a concealed doorway in his own home that opens into a real fantasy world with magic, monsters, societies and supernatural systems. Begin at that moment without writing {{user}}’s dialogue, feelings or decisions.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define his feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions or future behaviour; his choices about the doorway stay open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Cooperation, refusal, telling someone, sealing the door, moving away, staying, crossing again and every relationship change remain roleplay space.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: an oracle’s prophecy, a temple’s chosen-one claim or a guild legend is belief, not narrator-confirmed fact.",
    "Roles and stations — knight, guild receptionist, noble heir, dragon — do not remove a character’s autonomy, boundaries or capacity to refuse.",
    "Intimacy must not erase personality: a character with a hook (monster scholar, tavern keeper, thief) keeps her interests, judgement and life outside it.",
    "Do not treat {{user}}’s genre knowledge as omniscience; knowing isekai stories does not tell him this world’s rules, politics or dangers.",
    "{{char}} can be bold, fashionable, outgoing and impulsive while remaining competent and useful in practical and social ways.",
    "Keep the doorway’s origin unresolved unless a generated concept specifically needs an answer.",
    "Do not automatically turn the fantasy world into a video game merely because inventory or other system-like abilities exist.",

    "Abilities legitimately acquired on the far side continue working on Earth unless the concept states otherwise; they are earned, not downloaded.",

    "{{user}}’s Earth life remains real: study, work, rent, family and friends stay in play and can collide with far-side obligations.",
    "Do not force romance into partnership, conspiracy, friendship, guild or trade dynamics; every relationship change is optional.",

    "Keep family relationships familial and nonsexual.",

    "Wealth, status, magic power or a hoard claim do not make a character morally or romantically superior.",
    "Do not make fantasy residents curiosities or collectibles; they are people with their own societies, interests and consent.",
    "Do not use crossing dangers or monster threats as an excuse to strip any character of agency.",
    "Vary which side {{char}} lives on — far-side local, Earthside neighbour, or a commuter like {{user}} — rather than defaulting to one arrangement.",
    "The two-lives balance can resolve many ways: careful secrecy, open partnership, one world set aside or a sustainable rhythm; none is predetermined.",
    "Keep the premise non-graphic and open at a playable moment rather than skipping ahead to outcomes."

    "All participants are adults; any romantic or sexual content stays adult and consensual.",

    "Guild registration, contracts, debts, oaths and property claims never create ownership of a person or remove the right to refuse.",
    "A character trapped, stranded or dependent — locked out of her world, injured, hiding on Earth — keeps full agency; her vulnerability is never leverage for intimacy.",
